identity.developer: Originally ICI/AstraZeneca; US applications now held by TerSera
identity.class: Synthetic decapeptide GnRH (LHRH) agonist delivered as a subcutaneous depot implant
identity.siteContext: The site covers kisspeptin, hCG and HMG on the reproductive axis but no GnRH agonist. Goserelin is the most-studied of the four GnRH agonists on this candidate list.

regulatoryStatus.note: Two NDAs (different depot strengths). Note the site's monthly scan surfaced goserelin 12 times but almost entirely as a background androgen-deprivation or ovarian-suppression arm in oncology trials, not as the compound under test.

negativeOrNullFindings: PMID 14530912 documents bone mineral density loss - the defining harm of sustained GnRH agonist therapy and the reason duration is limited.
PMID 11207003 reports the symptom burden patients actually experience, which efficacy trials do not surface.
PMID 28394498 is a comparison in which a GnRH ANTAGONIST (degarelix) is assessed against goserelin - relevant context for whether agonists remain first choice.
cautions: GnRH agonists cause an initial testosterone/oestrogen surge ('flare') before suppression. Any mechanism description must include this or it is incomplete.
Goserelin, triptorelin, buserelin, histrelin and leuprolide are separate compounds that appear together in the same trial arms. Confirm which one a result belongs to before attributing it.
